1. Introduction.content:
Sidra Medicine vision is to become a beacon of learning, discovery, and exceptional care, ranked among the top academic medical centers in the world. One of Sidra's design principles is being a fully digital hospital that utilizes information, data, and insights to drive patient- care, clinical outcomes, research and operational efficiency.
Currently, there are several applications and platforms deployed at Sidra Medicine such as Cerner Electronic Medical Records (Cerner EMR), Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, Datix, Qualtrics and others which support daily clinical and administrative operations of the hospital and digitize patients' journey. Those applications generate massive volumes of data encompassing patient records, administrative information, financial transactions, quality related incidents, patient surveys and others. In addition, there are multiple Research platforms that generate data related to Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) and Genome reference data, Biorepository, phenotype data, clinical trials and clinical registries.
The dispersed and siloed nature of this data often hampers Sidra Medicine ability to timely extract meaningful insights, hindering swift decision-making and optimization of resources as significant number of man-hours spent on manually extracting reports from different applications as well as manually distribute them to different users.
By building a Data Lake and analytics solutions, Sidra Medicine aims to create a single source of truth and uncover actionable insights, predict trends, and align their strategies with real- time operational metrics. This empowers Sidra's Clinicians, Researchers and Executives to make informed, data-driven decisions that foster improved patient care, elevate financial and operational performance, and position the hospital at the forefront of healthcare innovation.

2. Objectives.content:
The primary objective of this project is to build a robust Data Lake and Analytics platform that enables efficient data extraction, transformation, and analysis of different data sources across Sidra Medicine.
Below are the business objectives and benefits that would be realized by the end of the project implementation:
Single Source of Truth: Consolidate disparate data sources into a single data lake.
Improved Decision-Making: Access to timely, accurate, and comprehensive insights to enable data driven decision-making at all levels of the organization, leading to better outcomes and strategies.
Operational Efficiency: Automated data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) processes reduce manual data entry and manipulation efforts, saving time and minimizing errors.
Strategic Planning and Budgeting: Accurate and comprehensive data supports effective strategic planning, budgeting, monitoring and allocation of resources for future growth and initiatives.
Effective Patient Care: Hospital staff can access and utilize a unified dashboard related to patient care, cost of treatment, patient experience and staffing utilization which aiding in care optimization and efficiency.
Unified Reporting and Analysis: Sidra executives, clinical and research staff can access integrated reports and dashboards that provide a holistic view of operations, finances, patient care, and other critical aspects.
Enhanced Performance Measurement: Key performance indicators (KPIs) can be monitored consistently, allowing the hospital to assess its performance and align activities with strategic objectives.
Reduced Data Latency: Real-time or near-real-time data updates allow for faster reporting, making critical information available for time-sensitive decisions.
Self-Service Analytics: Hospital staff can use user-friendly tools to perform ad hoc queries and analyses without needing extensive technical skills, promoting self-service data exploration and analysis.
Data Visualization: Interactive visualizations and dashboards provide intuitive ways to communicate complex data, enabling quicker understanding of trends and insights.
Data Governance and Security: The Data-Lake allows for centralized data governance, ensuring data security, privacy, access control, and compliance with regulatory standards and best practices (i.e. Role Based access control and data encryption).
Data Catalog and Metadata Management: The data-lake can provide a centralized repository to catalog and manage the metadata associated with the stored data.
Long-Term Data Retention: The data-lake provides a secure and accessible repository for historical data, ensuring valuable insights are retained even as ERP systems evolve.
Predictive Analytics, AI, and Machine Learning: The data-lake solution can provide a rich dataset and platforms for training predictive models, AI, and machine learning algorithms, and support data science workloads. It includes tools and frameworks for statistical analysis, machine learning, and AI.
Precision Medicine and Personalized Healthcare: The data-lake can support precision medicine initiatives by integrating genomics data, molecular profiling, and clinical data to identify biomarkers, develop targeted therapies, and personalize treatment plans based on an individual's unique characteristics and genetic makeup.

3. Scope of Work and Deliverables.content:
The scope of work includes the following:
1. Requirements gathering and analysis
2. Data-Lake / Data-Lakehouse architecture design
3. Infrastructure setup
4. Data ingestion and integration (both batch and real-time).
5. Data processing and transformation
6. Data storage and management
7. Data Governance and Compliance
8. Analytics, Reporting and Machine Learning models setup
9. Testing and validation
10. Documentation and training
The project major tasks and deliverables include the following:

3.1 Project Initiation and Requirements.content:
· Identify stakeholders and establish communication channels.
· Identify the list of data sources.
· Conduct meetings with stakeholders to gather data requirements, business objectives, analytics needs and Machine Learning use cases.
· Document stakeholder inputs and finalize the scope of the project including functional and non-functional requirements.
· Deliverable: Requirements Specification Document.

3.2 Data Lake / Lakehouse Architecture D.content:
" Design a robust data lake architecture that includes:
- Raw Data Zone: Ingest raw data from various sources.
- Cleansed Data Zone: Store cleansed and transformed data.
- Curated Data Zone: Organize data for specific analytical use cases
" Design a specific subject areas Data Marts for detailed analysis.
· Tools and Technologies
Utilize the following Azure services:
- Azure Databricks: For data processing and analytics.
- Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS): For scalable data storage.
- Azure Synapse Analytics: For data warehousing.
- Azure Data Factory: For data integration and orchestration.
- Azure Purview: for unified data governance
· Deliverable: detailed Data Architecture Desing document

3.3 Infrastructure Setup on Azure.content:
" Resource Provisioning
Provision and configure the following resources:
- Azure Databricks workspace
- Azure Data Lake Storage
- Azure Synapse Analytics
· Network Configuration
Ensure secure and efficient network setup:
- Virtual Network setup
- Network Security Groups
- Private Endpoints for secure data access
- Deliverable: Complete configuration and environment setup sign-off according to architectural design and best practice.

3.4 Data Ingestion and Integration.content:
· Data Ingestion
Implement data ingestion pipelines:
- Batch data ingestion using Azure Data Factory
- Real-time data ingestion using Azure Event Hubs and Stream Analytics
" Data Integration, Processing and Transformation
- Integrate data through ETL/ELT processes and perform data cleansing and transformation.
- Develop an efficient and optimized ETL/ELT pipeline. Deliverable: complete data integration and ELT/ELT pipelines.

3.5 Data Quality and Validation.content:
- Implement data quality checks and validation rules to ensure accuracy and consistency.
- Develop processes to identify and resolve data anomalies, duplicates, and discrepancies.
- Establish data profiling and monitoring mechanisms to ensure ongoing data quality.
- Deliverable: Data Quality and Validation Framework Implementation

3.6 Data Storage and Management.content:
- Organize data in Azure Data Lake Storage
- Optimize data storage in Azure Synapse Analytics (Tabe design, indexing and partitioning)

3.7 Data Governance and Compliance.content:
- Implement robust security measures and role-based access control.
- Implement core master data management capabilities.
- Implement Data Catalog and metadata management.
- Ensure the implementation compliance with local and international data security and privacy laws and frameworks.

3.8 Analytics, Reporting and Machine Lea.content:
- Ensure seamless integration with Sidra's existing PowerBI platform.
- Develop dashboards and operational reports for Finance, HR, Supply Chain and other subject areas covered by Oracle Fusion ERP data source.
- Configure Databricks SQL Analytics for querying
- Re-map existing PowerBI dashboards to the newly developed Data Marts.
- Configure Machine Learning platform and build few data models for both Clinical and Non-Clinical subject areas.

3.9 Testing and Quality Assurance.content:
- Perform unit testing of ETL scripts, data lake and data-warehouse components.
- Conduct integration testing to ensure seamless integration and end to end functionality.
- Validate Data-Lake accuracy and completeness against source systems data.
- Engage stakeholders in user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure the solution meets business requirements.
- Deliverable: Test Plans and Test Results

3.10 User Training and Documentation.content:
- Prepare user training materials and guides for data engineers and administrators.
- Develop standard operating procedures documents
- Prepare admin and support guides for the entire Data Lake Platform.
- Conduct training sessions for developers, engineers and end users.
- Create documentation for data dictionaries, ETL processes, data lineage, and best practices.
- Deliverable: User Training Materials and Documentation

3.11 Deployment and Go-Live.content:
- Plan the deployment of the Data Lake Platform to the production environment.
- Migrate the ETL processes, data, and configurations to the production environment.
- Monitor system performance during the initial period of usage.
- Address any issues or concerns that arise during deployment.
- Deliverable: Production Data Warehouse and Analytics Environment

3.12 Post-Implementation Support.content:
- Provide ongoing technical support to address any system issues, bugs, or enhancements.
- Monitor system performance, data quality, and user interactions.
- Implement updates and modifications based on evolving business requirements.
- Deliverable: Support and Maintenance Documentation

Status Meetings and Reports.content: the Vendor's Agreement Manager, the Sidra Senior or other Program Manager and other appropriate representatives of the Parties shall meet at a mutually agreed site or by teleconference, as requested by Sidra, to discuss the status of the project. During such status meetings, the Parties shall discuss, the status of the project and any difficulties or issues that may exist, and any proposed changes to dates generally and any Due Dates specifically. Vendor shall keep minutes of the meetings and shall issue minutes in draft form to all meeting attendees promptly following each meeting. Following its receipt thereof, the recipient promptly shall review and provide to the drafter any feedback and comments it may have with respect to such minutes, following which the drafter shall incorporate any feedback and comments into the minutes and re-issue the minutes in final form. At least two (2) business days before each such status meeting, Vendor shall present to Sidra a written report of the status of the project. The report shall include a summary in such detail as Sidra shall reasonably request of the accomplishments and difficulties encountered, suggestions and proposed actions for dealing with and resolving any identified difficulties and the anticipated results, and a comprehensive and consolidated log of all outstanding project-related problems identified by Sidra and Vendor that remain to be resolved. Sidra shall have the right to assume that Vendor is not aware of any problems, issues or risks unless Vendor specifically identifies such problems, issues or risks in the project status reports.

10. Pre-Live testing.content: Vendor shall arrange Pre-live testing ("Pre-Live Testing") in accordance with applicable Test Plan to be agreed by the parties. The Test Plan shall specify the relevant Acceptance Criteria including Data Quality and Dashboards performance metrics, and the sequence and the timings to be followed. Sidra shall report to Vendor any defects discovered during Pre-Live Testing, and Vendor promptly shall correct such defects. When Pre-Live Testing has been successfully concluded, Sidra shall so notify Vendor , and the Software thereafter will be ready for Production Use.

11. Production use.content:
Following successful completion of Pre-Live Testing, Sidra will deploy the Software in production. During the Production Use Period, Vendor shall work with Sidra to stabilize, and then optimize, the use of the Software. If any defects are discovered during the
10
Production Use Period, Sidra shall report such defects to Vendor, and Vendor promptly shall correct such defects. When the Production Use Period has been successfully concluded (all defects have been corrected), Sidra shall so notify Vendor.

12. Project Completion and Hand-Over.content:
Upon successful completion of the project, the project manager will facilitate a thorough review and verification of all deliverables to ensure they meet the defined acceptance criteria.
Each of the following conditions are required for a project to achieve "Project Completion": (a) the Production Use Period has been successfully completed; (b) Vendor has provided to Sidra all Documentation and other deliverables relating to the project. Nothing else, including Sidra's use of the Software, or any component thereof, in a live, production environment shall constitute Project Completion, affect any rights and remedies that may be available to Sidra and/or constitute or result in "acceptance" under general Agreement law or any other Law.
If the WORK has been performed and completed in accordance with the AGREEMENT, Sidra will issue a CERTIFICATE OF COMPLETION stating the COMPLETION DATE therein. Thereafter, Vendor shall commence providing Maintenance and Support services.

13. Warranty period for the software.content: The Warranty Period for the WORKS performed shall be twelve (12) months from project COMPLETION DATE, and VENDOR shall warrant that the WORKS shall be free from defects, errors and bad workmanship throughout the warranty period.
